title: The Scorpion and the Toad
novel:
Lily came back to New York. She stood at the apartment door, her suitcase [[trembling|tremble]] in her hand. "I made a [[mistake|mistake]]," she [[whispered|whisper]]. Marshall opened the door and froze. He had [[fantasized|fantasize]] about this moment for weeks, but now that it was real, he felt nothing but [[numbness|numb]].

Ted told Marshall to be [[cautious|cautious]]. "She broke your heart," he [[reminded|remind]]. Barney told the story of the [[scorpion|scorpion]] and the [[toad|toad]] — the scorpion stings because it's in its [[nature|nature]]. "Some people just sting," Barney said.

But Lily was [[determined|determine]] to win Marshall back. She cooked his favorite [[lasagna|lasagna]], cleaned the apartment, and even [[endured|endure]] Barney's [[insults|insult]]. Marshall watched her with a [[mixture|mixture]] of love and [[suspicion|suspicion]].

One night, Lily sat on the [[couch|couch]] and said, "I know I hurt you. I don't [[deserve|deserve]] a second chance. But I will spend the rest of my life trying to earn one." Her voice [[cracked|crack]].

Marshall was silent for a long time. Then he said, "I'm not ready to [[forgive|forgive]] you yet. But I'm not ready to let you go either." It wasn't a happy ending — not yet — but it was a [[beginning|beginning]].

tremble.en: to shake slightly, especially because you are nervous or scared

mistake.en: something that you do that is not right

whisper.en: to speak very quietly so that only someone close can hear

fantasize.en: to think about something very pleasant that is unlikely to happen

numb.en: unable to feel anything; emotionally frozen

cautious.en: careful to avoid danger or risk

scorpion.en: a small creature with a poisonous tail that curves over its back

toad.en: an animal like a frog with drier, rougher skin

nature.en: a person's basic character or the basic quality of something

determine.en: to decide firmly to do something

lasagna.en: an Italian dish of flat pasta with meat, cheese and sauce

endure.en: to suffer something painful or difficult without complaining

insult.en: a rude remark that hurts someone's feelings

mixture.en: a combination of different things or feelings

suspicion.en: a feeling that someone has done something wrong

couch.en: a long comfortable seat for two or more people

deserve.en: to have earned something because of your actions or qualities

crack.en: to break; (of voice) to sound rough and uncontrolled

forgive.en: to stop being angry with someone who has done something wrong
